newsitem.title: MEXICO: Greater reserves would benefit Mexico - Mancera.
newsitem.headline: Greater reserves would benefit Mexico - Mancera.

text.p: Mexico could benefit from a higher level of international reserves, Banco de Mexico governor Miguel Mancera said on Saturday.
In a speech to the annual meeting of the Institute of Mexican Financial Executives, Mancera noted that greater reserves result in lower interest rates on external credits.
"I think that at the present moment it is suitable for Mexico to increase its central bank reserves in both definitions," Mancera said.
Mexico defines its reserves according to the law governing the bank and as well by International Monetary Fund (IMF) standards.

At November 22, the reserves under Banco de Mexico's definition, were $16.257 billion. Under the IMF definition, which mainly removes the money that the Banco de Mexico owes it, the reserves were $4.724 billion
Mancera defended the level of the reserves, saying that they compared favourably with levels in many industrialized nations.
He said that under the IMF definition, Mexico's reserves had grown by $4.695 billion from the start of the year to last week.
The central bank also recently started a dollar option program that allows it to purchase dollars on the open market without seeming to intervene in the exchange market.
